transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: We need to build an AI-based resume analyzer that can automatically shortlist candidates for our software engineering roles.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: Okay. How should the system decide which candidates to shortlist?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: It should rank them based on relevance to the job description.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: How are we defining relevance?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: Mainly skills and experience. And overall profile strength.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: What does overall profile strength include?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: Things like good companies, solid projects, impactful work.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: Should we prioritize years of experience?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: Yes, but not strictly. Sometimes a strong fresher is better than someone with 5 average years.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: Do we have historical hiring data to train the system?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: We have past resumes and hiring decisions, but they're not very structured.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: How accurate should the system be?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: It should be good enough so that HR trusts it.
ambiguousPhrases: good enough so that HR trusts it

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: Do we need explainability? For example, why a candidate was ranked higher?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: Yes, that would be useful.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: Are there any constraints regarding bias or fairness?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: Yes, we must avoid bias, especially related to gender or college background.
ambiguousPhrases: especially related to gender or college background

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: Should the system process resumes in real-time or batch mode?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: It shouldn't be slow.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: What is the expected response time per resume?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: Ideally quick.

transcript.speaker: ML Engineer
transcript.text: What is the timeline for delivery?

transcript.speaker: Hiring Manager
transcript.text: We need an MVP soon.

clarifications.question: What is the precise latency threshold for single resume parsing and batch screening?
clarifications.triggeredBy: It shouldn't be slow / Ideally quick
options: Single resume < 1.5 seconds, batch of 100 resumes < 30 seconds
Single resume < 5 seconds, batch of 500 resumes < 5 minutes
Real-time streaming parsing < 500ms per resume
clarifications.selectedResponse: Single resume parsing must be under 1.5s (95th percentile) and batch upload of 100 resumes must complete within 30 seconds.

clarifications.question: How should bias mitigation be enforced and measured across gender and educational background?
clarifications.triggeredBy: Yes, we must avoid bias, especially related to gender or college background.
options: Pre-processing anonymization (mask name, gender, college tier) + Disparate Impact Ratio >= 0.80
Post-processing calibration across demographic bins with statistical parity
Blind screening with adversarial debiasing in embedding layer
clarifications.selectedResponse: Anonymize PII and college names before scoring; enforce Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR) between 0.80 and 1.25 across gender and college tiers.

clarifications.question: What quantifiable accuracy metric defines 'good enough for HR trust' for candidate shortlisting?
clarifications.triggeredBy: It should be good enough so that HR trusts it.
options: Top-10 Ranking Precision >= 85% and Recall@20 >= 80% compared to senior technical recruiter consensus
F1-Score >= 0.90 across all shortlisted candidates
Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) >= 0.75 on historical test sets
clarifications.selectedResponse: Top-10 shortlisting Precision >= 85% and NDCG@10 >= 0.82 evaluated against blind human recruiter consensus.

clarifications.question: What specific explainability format is required for why a candidate is ranked or disqualified?
options: SHAP/feature breakdown showing matched skills %, years of relevant experience, and key project impact badges
Textual bullet points highlighting top 3 strengths and missing prerequisite skills
Interactive match scorecard with side-by-side JD skill overlap
clarifications.selectedResponse: Provide a structured breakdown for each candidate: matched required skills %, matched preferred skills %, quantified project score, and 3 bullet justifications for ranking.

clarifications.question: What resume file formats, parsing schemas, and unstructured historical data cleanup methods must be supported?
clarifications.triggeredBy: We have past resumes and hiring decisions, but they're not very structured.
options: Support PDF, DOCX, TXT up to 10MB; OCR fallback; semi-automated labeling pipeline for historical resumes
Only PDF support with structured JSON resume format export
Multi-lingual resume extraction with cloud OCR API
clarifications.selectedResponse: Support PDF and DOCX up to 10MB; parse unstructured text into standardized JSON schema (skills, education, work history, projects); run automated data cleaning on historical logs.

clarifications.question: How should 'profile strength' (good companies, solid projects) and freshers vs experienced candidates be weighted?
clarifications.triggeredBy: Things like good companies, solid projects, impactful work / Sometimes a strong fresher is better than someone with 5 average years.
options: Dynamic weighted scoring: 40% Verified Project Complexity & Skills, 30% Job Relevance, 20% Impact/Achievements, 10% Years of Exp with fresher bonus
Fixed rule filter based on company tier list and minimum 3 years experience
Pure semantic embedding similarity score without separate company weighting
clarifications.selectedResponse: Weighting formula: 45% Skill Match & Demonstrated Tech Stack, 35% Project Impact & Scope (open source, deployed apps), 20% Relevant Experience; allow freshers with high project scores to outrank generic profiles.

clarifications.question: What is the concrete deadline and core scope for the 'MVP soon' deliverable?
options: 4-week MVP deliverable: Web dashboard, single & batch resume upload (PDF/DOCX), scoring engine, explainability breakdown, and CSV export
2-week prototype with basic keyword matching
8-week production release with ATS integration
clarifications.selectedResponse: MVP delivery in 4 weeks: Web-based candidate shortlisting portal supporting PDF/DOCX ingestion, JD matching, top-N ranking with explainability cards, and fairness metrics dashboard.
